note: ELA.K.R.1.2 and ELA.K.R.2.3 do not exist at kindergarten; CPALMS ids skip them.

ELA.K.F.1.1.text: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic concepts of print.

sub: Blend and segment syllables in spoken words.
Identify and produce alliterative and rhyming words.
Blend and segment onset and rimes of single-syllable words.
Identify the initial, medial, and final sound of spoken words.
Add or delete phonemes at the beginning or end of a spoken word and say the resulting word.
Segment and blend phonemes in single-syllable spoken words.

ELA.K.F.1.3.text: Use knowledge of grade-appropriate phonics and word-analysis skills to decode words accurately.
sub: Demonstrate knowledge of the most frequent sound for each consonant.
Demonstrate knowledge of the short and long sounds for the five major vowels.

ELA.K.F.1.4.text: Recognize and read with automaticity grade-level high frequency words.

ELA.K.R.1.1.text: Describe the main character(s), setting, and important events in a story.

ELA.K.R.1.3.text: Explain the roles of author and illustrator of a story.

ELA.K.R.2.1.text: Use titles, headings, and illustrations to predict and confirm the topic of texts.

ELA.K.R.2.2.text: Identify the topic of and multiple details in a text.

ELA.K.R.2.4.text: Explain the difference between opinions and facts about a topic.

ELA.K.V.1.1.text: Use grade-level academic vocabulary appropriately in speaking and writing.

ELA.K.V.1.2.text: Ask and answer questions about unfamiliar words in grade-level content.

ELA.K.V.1.3.text: Identify and sort common words into basic categories, relating vocabulary to background knowledge.

MA.K.NSO.1.1.text: Given a group of up to 20 objects, count the number of objects in that group and represent the number of objects with a written numeral. State the number of objects in a rearrangement of that group without recounting.

MA.K.NSO.1.2.text: Given a number from 0 to 20, count out that many objects.

MA.K.NSO.1.3.text: Identify positions of objects within a sequence using the words first, second, third, fourth or fifth.

MA.K.NSO.1.4.text: Compare the number of objects from 0 to 20 in two groups using the terms less than, equal to or greater than.

MA.K.NSO.2.1.text: Recite the number names to 100 by ones and by tens. Starting at a given number, count forward within 100 and backward within 20.

MA.K.NSO.2.2.text: Represent whole numbers from 10 to 20, using a unit of ten and a group of ones, with objects, drawings and expressions or equations.

MA.K.NSO.2.3.text: Locate, order and compare numbers from 0 to 20 using the number line and terms less than, equal to or greater than.

MA.K.NSO.3.1.text: Explore addition of two whole numbers from 0 to 10, and related subtraction facts.

MA.K.NSO.3.2.text: Add two one-digit whole numbers with sums from 0 to 10 and subtract using related facts with procedural reliability.

MA.K.AR.1.1.text: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number.

MA.K.AR.1.2.text: Given a number from 0 to 10, find the different ways it can be represented as the sum of two numbers.

MA.K.AR.1.3.text: Solve addition and subtraction real-world problems using objects, drawings or equations to represent the problem.

MA.K.AR.2.1.text: Explain why addition or subtraction equations are true using objects or drawings.

MA.K.M.1.1.text: Identify the attributes of a single object that can be measured such as length, volume or weight.

MA.K.M.1.2.text: Directly compare two objects that have an attribute which can be measured in common. Express the comparison using language to describe the difference.

MA.K.M.1.3.text: Express the length of an object, up to 20 units long, as a whole number of lengths by laying non-standard objects end to end with no gaps or overlaps.

MA.K.GR.1.1.text: Identify two- and three-dimensional figures regardless of their size or orientation. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.

MA.K.GR.1.2.text: Compare two-dimensional figures based on their similarities, differences and positions. Sort two-dimensional figures based on their similarities and differences. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles and squares.

MA.K.GR.1.3.text: Compare three-dimensional figures based on their similarities, differences and positions. Sort three-dimensional figures based on their similarities and differences. Figures are limited to spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.

MA.K.GR.1.4.text: Find real-world objects that can be modeled by a given two- or three-dimensional figure. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.

MA.K.GR.1.5.text: Combine two-dimensional figures to form a given composite figure. Figures used to form a composite shape are limited to triangles, rectangles and squares.

MA.K.DP.1.1.text: Collect and sort objects into categories and compare the categories by counting the objects in each category. Report the results verbally, with a written numeral or with drawings.
